hints: Notice the engine ejects $90 \text{ kg}$ every second at $190 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ - so find the momentum carried away per second.
Recall force equals rate of change of momentum, $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$, which for a steady exhaust is mass per second multiplied by exhaust velocity.
Calculate $(90)(190)$ in newtons, then divide by $1000$ to get kilonewtons and keep two significant figures.
walkthrough: Identify the given rate: mass ejected per unit time is $\Delta m / \Delta t = 90 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$ and exhaust speed relative to rocket is $v = 190 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
State the rule: the force on the gas equals its rate of gain of momentum, and by Newton's third law the rocket feels an equal opposite thrust, so $F = (\Delta m / \Delta t) v$.
Substitute with units: $F = (90 \text{ kg s}^{-1})(190 \text{ m s}^{-1}) = 17100 \text{ kg m s}^{-2} = 17100 \text{ N}$.
Convert to kilonewtons: $17100 \text{ N} / 1000 = 17.1 \text{ kN}$, which to two significant figures is $17 \text{ kN}$.

options.A: Divides $190 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ by $90 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$ to give about $2.1 \text{ kN}$, which reverses the momentum-rate relationship.
options.B: Equals the rate of momentum given to the gas, $(90 \text{ kg s}^{-1})(190 \text{ m s}^{-1}) = 17100 \text{ N} \approx 17 \text{ kN}$.
options.C: Rounds $17.1 \text{ kN}$ incorrectly upward to $18 \text{ kN}$ instead of keeping two significant figures as $17 \text{ kN}$.
options.D: Is about ten times too large at $162 \text{ kN}$, from a power-of-ten error when converting $17100 \text{ N}$ to kilonewtons.
